analysis: The host completed training and independent validation successfully, reporting macro HR@10=0.6038 across four categories: Movies_and_TV 0.640, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.635, Electronics 0.455, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.685. Electronics was the weakest category. The run used 1068.87 allocated GPU-seconds. REMAINING_GPU_SECONDS now has a finite, validated 1800-second fallback, and exceptions are saved under working/training_error.txt; the successful result does not establish whether the fallback was exercised or caused recovery. No expert ablations or comparable prior host results were supplied, so the benefit of fusion and full-history reconstruction remains unproven.
code_summary: Each category trains two independent experts with seed 42: a residual MultVAE with 256 hidden units and 64 latent dimensions, and a two-block SASRec with default hidden size 50 and sequence length 200. MultVAE reconstructs the complete binary history from a randomly retained half-history context using multinomial likelihood plus annealed KL loss. SASRec uses chronological next-item training with one sampled negative and binary cross-entropy. Each expert selects its checkpoint by validation HR@10, breaking ties with NDCG@10. Inference averages their candidate ranks with equal weights. The generated predictor restores both saved architectures and preserves all four dataset routes. Training retains the supplied splits, GAGC_DATA_DIR, single-GPU execution, category budget allocation, and checkpoint/export agreement checks.
